# African startups raise $3.02B in 10 months
[Joseph Oloyede](https://insights.techcabal.com/profile/joseph-oloyede/)

![Ecllipse](https://insights.techcabal.com/wp-content/themes/tcinsight/images/dot.png)

##### Published 9th NOVEMBER 2026
African startups raised $3.02B across the first 10 months of 2026, with October securing $540M.

Across the first ten months of 2026, African startups raised $3.02 billion, representing a 14.2% year-on-year growth compared to the $2.65 billion raised during the same period in 2025. In October alone, startups secured $540 million across 73 disclosed deals, surpassing the $442 million recorded in October 2025 and closing out the month with a mega-deal.

## Monthly funding breakdown: 2025 vs. 2026 (January – October)
2025 vs. 2026 (funding October 2026)

## October top funded: OPay, MNT-Halan, and healthcare lead big deals
- OPay (Nigeria) secured a massive [$185 million](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-09/softbank-backed-opay-wins-185-million-standard-bank-placement?) private placement from Standard Bank Group ahead of its planned US listing.
- MNT-Halan (Egypt) pulled in $119.34 million across two major transactions securing an [$82 million](https://techbuild.africa/egyptian-fintech-mnt-halans-82m-planned-ipo/) debt facility from Tasheel Finance and Halan Consumer Finance, alongside a [$37.34 million](https://launchbaseafrica.com/2026/10/05/mnt-halan-ipo/) anchor equity investment from Egypt’s CIB as it prepares for its IPO.
- ABA Life (Morocco) raised [$40 million](https://en.arageek.com/aba-life-secures-40m-to-drive-moroccos-healthtech-to-global-stage) in equity from Admaius Capital Partners to scale its integrated AI and medical technology solutions.
- Healthleap (South Africa) pulled in [$38 million](https://african-startups.com/countries/south-africa/south-africa-founded-healthleap-raises-38-million-to-help-hospitals-detect-missed-diagnoses-with-ai/) in Seed and Series A funding from Sequoia Capital, First Round Capital, and Hummingbird Ventures.
- Max (Nigeria) raised a [$29 million](https://nithio.com/nithio-expands-its-e-mobility-portfolio-with-investment-in-max/) Series B3 round from Nithio to expand its electric mobility infrastructure.

![](https://insights.techcabal.com/wp-content/uploads/insight/2026/11/SOTIA-H1-2026-15-819x1024.webp)

- Bisedge Holdings (Nigeria) secured [$11.2 million](https://innovation-village.com/finnfund-commits-e10-million-to-bisedge-holdings-for-african-ev-logistics-expansion/) in debt from Finnfund for its EV logistics and outsourcing operations.
- Beacon Power Services (Nigeria) added a [$10 million](https://www.techinafrica.com/ebrd-backs-nigerian-energy-startup-beacon-power-services-in-20-9-million-grid-modernisation-project/) debt facility from the EBRD for grid modernisation.
- EASE Holdings BV (Pan-African) raised [$9.5 million](https://www.africaglobalfunds.com/news/private-equity/deals/aafc-group-invests-95-million-in-ease/) in equity from AAFC Group for its healthcare equipment-as-a-service model.
- Satlyt (Kenya) secured an [$8 million](https://empowerafrica.com/kenyan-founded-satlyt-raises-8-million-to-expand-ai-software-for-satellites/) seed round from Non Sibi Ventures for its satellite computing software.

## **Top funding destinations**
Nigeria remains the most funded market on the continent, attracting $688 million between January and October 2026.

[Share on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=252296078952383&display=popup&href=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcabal.com%2F2026%2F08%2F10%2Fafrican-vc-funding-squeez%2F)[Share on Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcabal.com%2F2026%2F08%2F10%2Fafrican-vc-funding-squeez%2F&text=What%20African%20investors%20think%20about%20the%20funding%20squeeze%20killing%20early-stage%20startups)[Share on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcabal.com%2F2026%2F08%2F10%2Fafrican-vc-funding-squeez%2F&title=What%20African%20investors%20think%20about%20the%20funding%20squeeze%20killing%20early-stage%20startups&summary=Startups%20raising%20between%20%24100%2C000%20and%20%241%20million%20fell%2044%25%20in%20six%20months.%20African%20VC%20investors%20explain%20what%20changed.)[Share on WhatsApp](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcabal.com%2F2026%2F08%2F10%2Fafrican-vc-funding-squeez%2F)[Share on Email](mailto:?body=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcabal.com%2F2026%2F08%2F10%2Fafrican-vc-funding-squeez%2F&subject=What%20African%20investors%20think%20about%20the%20funding%20squeeze%20killing%20early-stage%20startups)

TechCabal Insights’ [State of Tech in Africa](https://techcabal.com/2026/07/21/state-of-tech-in-africa-h1-2026-recap-is-consolidation-the-new-growth-story/) report puts funding in H1 2026 at $1.44 billion, up 1.4% year on year.

[Africa: The Big Deal,](https://thebigdeal.substack.com/) which tracks the market using a different methodology, found that only 190 startups raised at least $100,000 in the first half of 2026, the lowest half-year count since 2021.

Pre-seed investing has changed over the last three or four years. Now, at pre-seed, people expect a startup to be doing maybe $1,500 to $2,000 a month and growing that at 10% to 20% month on month.

As rates rose and capital tightened, investor priorities recalibrated. Greater emphasis was laid on things that demonstrated likely venture-scale outcomes, such as business performance, distribution, and a demonstrable line of sight to exponential growth and exit opportunities.

Pre-seed investors still exist in Africa.

I would like to see more corporate venture capital at the pre-seed stage.

Funds are also growing.

Rather than focusing primarily on helping companies raise their next round, we should help founders build businesses that can survive longer without relying on continuous fundraising.

# Egyptian startup Fincart raises $2.8 million to expand AI commerce platform
28th Jul, 2026

Launch Africa, a pan-African venture capital fund, and Antler MENAP, the early-stage fund focused on the Middle East, North Africa, and Pakistan regions, co-led the funding round, with participation from Yango Ventures, Five35 Ventures, Bluestream Capital, Hi2 Global, Kalahari Venture Labs, and other unnamed investors.

The raise comes 18 months after Fincart’s [undisclosed pre-seed round](https://www.wamda.com/2025/01/egypt-fincart-secures-pres-seed-round-led-plus-vc) and coincides with the startup’s pivot from a logistics management platform into an AI-powered operating system for e-commerce merchants.

Fincart said part of the funding will finance its expansion beyond Egypt from 2027. For Launch Africa, the investment is a bet on the region’s commerce infrastructure rather than a single startup.

Q1-Q3 2025 vs. 2026

2026

Q1Q2Q3$559M$559M$963M$963M$785M$785M$768M$768M$693M$693M$1025M$1025M

While overall transaction volume dropped in the first half of the year, funding activity rebounded sharply in Q3 2026. Q3 alone brought in $1.025 billion across 167 deals, up from $785 million across 149 deals in Q3 2025, driven by stronger deal flow and larger growth rounds.

![](https://c76c7bbc41.mjedge.net/wp-content/uploads/tc/2026/10/SOTIA-H1-2026-11-819x1024.webp)

Nigeria remains Africa’s top funding destination so far in 2026, pulling in $624 million across the first nine months.

- Ventures Platform completed an [$84 million](https://www.venturesplatform.com/stories/ventures-platform-closes-pan-african-fund-ii-at-84m) second close for its Pan-African Fund II, backed by Norfund and the European Bank.
- CardinalStone Capital Advisers hit a [$76 million](https://cardinalstonepe.com/cardinalstone-capital-advisers-cca-announces-first-close-of-cca-growth-fund-ii-ccagf-ii/) first close for its West Africa SME growth fund.
